tasks.title: Add hub client call that opens the events route and classifies its answers
steps: Write TS-18-1..6 in internal/hub (httptest servers) and confirm they fail

Add internal/hub/events.go with Client.Events(ctx, pat, slug) returning a stream reader type (stub the reader body for now); build GET /api/v1/events?workspace=<url.QueryEscape(slug)> with Authorization Bearer, Accept text/event-stream and the client's User-Agent

Copy the client's HTTP settings as send does: no redirects, but bound only the wait for response headers with the ordinary 10 s bound (e.g. a ResponseHeaderTimeout or a timer cancelling until headers arrive) and read the body with no overall timeout until ctx ends; make the header bound overridable in tests

Classify non-200 answers through the existing classify/errorObject helpers: 401 -> ErrRefused, 403 -> ErrForbidden with a message naming audit:read and PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}, 404 -> ErrNotFound, other 4xx except 429 -> *RejectedError with Status/Code/Message
Treat 429, 5xx, transport failures, timeouts, redirects and a 200 whose content type is not text/event-stream as *UnavailableError (Status 0 for transport failures)
Pass every returned error through scrubbed so the PAT never appears in error text
Define exported event-type constants for hub.forge.issue.labeled and hub.forge.issue.closed in internal/hub

tasks.title: Implement the SSE frame reader, event decoding and the fake hub's event stream
steps: Write TS-18-7..13 and confirm they fail

In internal/hub/events.go implement the frame reader copying internal/afclient/sse.go's rules (do not import it): id:/event:/data: fields, data lines joined with a line break, colon lines as comments, CRLF and LF, a frame with no data is no event, a line longer than 1 MiB ends the read with an error and delivers no further frames

Expose each frame and each comment to the caller as activity (a callback or a returned item kind) and decode a JSON-object frame into a typed value StreamEvent{ID, Type, Workspace, Issue int, Label string}; use JSON id else frame id:, JSON event_type else frame event:, workspace slug when hub names one, issue from payload.issue (integer) / payload.issue.number / payload.number, label from payload.label (string) / payload.label.name; a frame whose data is not a JSON object is activity only (name the type so it does not clash with the existing hub.Event)
Keep all hub field names in internal/hub

Add internal/hub/fakehub/events.go serving /api/v1/events from route() in fakehub.go: apply the usual token access check (refuse), honour Inject/Fail/Hangup on the path, else answer 200 text/event-stream and hold the connection open, recording its workspace

Add exported fakehub seams: SendEvent(workspace, event), Heartbeat(workspace) (an SSE comment), EndEvents(workspace), EventConns(workspace) int, an EventsRequests count helper, and EmitLabeledOnAdd(bool) so that a label added through the forge API (ws.relabel) sends hub.forge.issue.labeled to every open connection of the workspace; add a helper to close an issue as a person (state closed) if none exists
Document the seams in a comment; docs/development.md is updated in the integration task

tasks.title: Make an issue-closed cancel remove its status labels and add none (worker and cleanup)
steps: Write TS-18-61..64 and confirm they fail

tasks.title: Start one event stream per poll loop with its connection sequence, poll switch and id expiry
steps: Write TS-18-14..19,21,22,24,48 (poll package, harness with fakehub event seams) and confirm they fail

Add internal/service/poll/stream.go: a stream goroutine per loop registered in Supervisor's s.wg with the loop's ctx; loop gains the cancel func and last-seen subscription UpdatedAt; startLoop starts the stream, forget/cancel of a loop stops it, Stop cancels streams and any handler and returns after they return

Each connection: Store token read, Hub.ResolvedVars, parseInterval (zero => open no connection, reread 5 minutes later on the poll clock), Hub.WorkspaceRecord, then Hub.Events at once with no random delay; record the reading time in stream state; log nothing about AF_POLL_INTERVAL
On a scan finding a changed UpdatedAt, close the open connection so the stream reconnects at once with the new token

On ErrNotSubscribed from the store stop the stream and call forget so the poll loop goes with it; a later scan restarts both; ErrUnreadable logs one ERROR naming the token read and keeps retrying (use a stream-owned failures set separate from the cycle's; basic reconnect-wait of 1 s is enough here, full backoff comes in the next task)
Have scan delete af_hub_events rows older than 7 days by the supervisor's clock
Read the open frames in a loop (no event handling yet beyond activity) and return when the ctx ends or the server ends the stream

tasks.title: Stream backoff, idle limit, recovery and connection-failure logging
steps: Write TS-18-25..32,36 and confirm they fail

Implement backoff on the poll clock: waits 1 s doubling to 60 s with no jitter after a failed or ended connection; after hub is found not to serve the stream (404 or 405 on the events route after the record read) every wait is 60 s; the first frame or comment of a connection resets the wait to 1 s; do not bring the poll's next cycle forward

Implement the 60 s idle limit: any received byte (frame, comment, heartbeat) rearms it, time spent acting on an event does not count (pause the idle timer while a handler runs); an idle connection is closed and treated as ended

Add a connection-failure record set to stream state, separate from the cycle's failures and the event-handling records, reusing classify/report from failure.go: ERROR for refused/forbidden token, hub not finding the workspace at the record read, rejected request or unreadable token, naming the operation and the PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug} route or the scope audit:read; WARN for unavailable; logged once per kind and operation until the next activity
Log one WARN that hub does not serve the event stream and labels are found by the poll alone for 404/405 after the record read (ERROR is not used)
The first frame or comment after logged failures or an outage logs one INFO that the stream recovered and resets the connection-failure records so a later failure logs again
Log one outage WARN when no connection with activity has lasted longer than the last-read poll interval (5 minutes if none read), not while the not-served WARN stands
Make sure no log record contains the PAT (errors come scrubbed from internal/hub)
done_when: no stream log record mentions AF_POLL_INTERVAL

tasks.title: Handle request events: filtering, poll-on check, issue read and new jobs
steps: Write TS-18-20,23,33,34,35,37,38,39 and confirm they fail

Add internal/service/poll/handle.go: on each decoded event, decide its kind; a request event is hub.forge.issue.labeled whose label EqualFold <prefix>triage or <prefix>fix (read the subscription's label_prefix each time) naming no other workspace; closed events go to the closed handler (next tasks); everything else is ignored with no hub request and logged at DEBUG at most

Malformed events (labeled with a request label, or closed, with no id, no issue number, an id over 256 bytes or with control characters) are ignored with no hub request and logged once per connection at WARN
Handle events of one workspace one at a time in arrival order (the stream goroutine handles inline); different workspaces never wait on each other

Handling a request: under the per-workspace lock skip a recorded id, ensure the poll is on (reread AF_POLL_INTERVAL when the stream's reading is older than 5 minutes; if it reads 0, act on nothing, record nothing, close the connection and reread after 5 minutes), build the forge client (Hub.Forge with pat, slug, repo from the connection), ReadIssue and stop if the issue is closed, a pull request, or lacks the label (EqualFold)
Otherwise call the refactored cycleRun.issue rules with the canonical label and Source {kind:event, by:<event id>}: a new request writes the poll record before removing the label

Add an event-handling failure record set (separate from connection and cycle records), classified like connection failures, logged once per kind and operation until an event of the workspace is handled without failure; such failures neither end the connection nor touch the connection records
done_when: a stream-made job has source {kind:event,by:evt-1} and request_label af:fix

tasks.title: Apply the poll's absorb, hold, owed and refusal rules to events and record event ids
steps: Write TS-18-40..47 and confirm they fail

Make the stream's call into cycleRun.issue exercise absorbed (open job of that kind or a duplicate refusal from Create: remove the label, or owe the removal on failure), held (do nothing, record the id) and already-taken/owed (remove again, no job) exactly as a cycle does

Handle jobs-layer refusals: ErrNotSubscribed ends handling with no label written and nothing recorded or logged as a failure; any other refusal is an event-handling failure at WARN with the label left and no id recorded
Handle hub failures (variable read, issue read, removal): leave the event to the poll, record no id, log an event-handling failure; a failed removal after a job was made leaves the removal owed

Record the event id in af_hub_events with taken_at from the supervisor's clock once an event is decided (job made, label absorbed or removed again, hold left alone, nothing to do per hub's issue read); do not record ignored events, closed events without an open job, events not acted on because the poll is off, or failed handling
Check the id in af_hub_events before acting, so a repeat (also after reopening the state file) sends no forge request
done_when: a repeated event id sends no forge request

tasks.title: Handle closed events: cancel an issue's open jobs; stream/poll race and reopen cases
steps: Write TS-18-52,53,54,55,56,66 and confirm they fail

In handle.go, for a closed event that is not malformed and names no other workspace, under the per-workspace lock: skip a recorded id, then look up the workspace's open jobs (queued/running/blocked, triage or fix, any source) of that issue number through the poll Jobs interface; with none stop with nothing recorded, no hub request and no log above DEBUG
Otherwise ensure the poll is on, read the issue through hub; an issue read as open cancels nothing (record the id as decided)

If the issue read fails, cancel nothing, record nothing and log an event-handling failure; a CancelIssue error after retries is an event-handling failure too and the jobs run on
Verify the reopened-and-relabelled case: a new request event makes a new job and a poll cycle with no event does too, because note treats issue_closed jobs as ended with no hold
Write the 50-round stream-vs-cycle race test (TS-18-52) with removal lag; fix any gap so every round ends with exactly one job and the label removed (run with -race)
